strengths: Novel extension of function vectors from LLMs to LMMs with rigorous causal mediation analysis to identify attention heads encoding spatial relations
Comprehensive experimental design with both synthetic and real datasets, thorough ablation studies examining layer effects, head set size, and context size
Strong fine-tuning results showing ~2× improvement over zero-shot baselines and outperformance of 4-shot ICL on synthetic data, demonstrating extractable vectors are optimizable
Clever demonstration of compositional generalization—relation-specific vectors linearly combine to solve untrained spatial relations (e.g., above-left)
Excellent reproducibility practices with detailed supplementary materials, dataset construction details, and promised code release
weaknesses: Extremely limited architectural scope: only OpenFlamingo-4B (4B params) tested; generalization to larger/different LMM architectures with different fusion mechanisms is unknown
Narrow task domain: only 4 basic spatial relations explored; unclear whether approach generalizes to semantic, temporal, causal, or functional relations
Low absolute performance on realistic data: GQA results show 5-45% accuracy across relations; weak performance on several relations limits practical utility
Weak baselines and missing comparisons: no comparison to LoRA, adapters, or other parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods; makes it unclear if FVs offer advantages over simpler alternatives

Computational cost unaddressed: causal mediation requires multiple forward passes per head; no analysis of computational overhead vs. alternatives; overall pipeline (extraction + identification + fine-tuning) complexity not justified

Hyperparameter selection lacks justification: different injection layers for synthetic (19) vs. real (8) data without clear rationale; potential data leakage if chosen on test sets; top-10 head selection appears arbitrary
Insufficient statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests; small test set (100 real images) makes uncertainty substantial; results presented as single runs

Composite function vector weighting (Eq. 5-6) lacks theoretical justification; unclear why prediction probability should be preferred over AIE scores; analogy results are weak (16.8% vs. similarly weak baselines)
Limited real-world validation: heavily curated GQA subset (201/113K images); no evaluation on standard vision-language benchmarks; unclear performance on uncurated diverse data

strengths: Novel extension of function vectors to multimodal models with rigorous causal mediation analysis using Average Indirect Effect (AIE)
Comprehensive ablation studies examining injection layer, head set size, and context size effects
Clear methodology with well-designed synthetic experiments demonstrating sparse causal subnetworks for spatial relations
Interesting proof-of-concept for linear combination of vectors to solve analogy problems with untrained relations
Reproducible research with detailed supplementary material and promised code release
Well-written presentation with effective visualizations of concepts and methodology
weaknesses: Real-world validation severely limited: GQA dataset contains only 201 images (~101 for training), with ~8 relation instances per category—insufficient for reliable conclusions
Unfair experimental comparisons: fine-tuned vectors use 1000 training examples while 4-shot ICL uses only demonstrations; claims about sample efficiency are misleading

Suspicious baseline results for analogy tasks: 1-shot ICL achieves 8.3% while 4-shot achieves 8.1% and 10-shot 9.6%—performance should not decrease with more examples, raising experimental validity concerns

Severely limited scope: only 4 basic spatial relations in main experiments, single relatively small model tested (OpenFlamingo-4B, 3B language component); generalization to larger models or non-spatial relations completely unexplored

Lack of statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing despite apparent variability; GQA results show 5-10x performance variation across relations without investigation

Methodological concerns: (1) summing mean activations for function vectors is ad-hoc without justification, (2) composite vector weighting is circular—using model's own uncertainties to define intervention, (3) causal analysis assumptions not fully justified for multimodal inputs
Composite vectors tested only on synthetic data with extremely simple compositional structure (above-left); applicability to complex real-world analogy unclear
Missing critical analysis: no explanation for dramatic performance differences across GQA relations; 'in front of' achieves only 5-10% accuracy suggesting task mismatch or dataset issues
Limited architectural exploration: claims about LMMs based on single model; unclear if findings transfer to larger or differently-trained vision-language models
Insufficient comparison with related work: no comparison with other mechanistic interpretability approaches or vector-based steering methods beyond baseline ICL

strengths: Novel extension of function vectors framework from LLMs to multimodal models with rigorous causal mediation analysis
Thorough experimental validation with comprehensive ablation studies examining layer effects, head set size, and context sensitivity
Clear demonstration that spatial relations are encoded in sparse, localized attention heads concentrated in intermediate layers
Shows multimodal function vectors capture meaningful, transferable representations that can be fine-tuned with modest data while keeping model frozen
Well-written paper with clear presentation, effective visualizations (Figures 2-3 particularly effective), and honest discussion of limitations
Solid reproducibility with detailed dataset construction, full hyperparameter specification, and promised code release
Interesting finding that relation-specific vectors can be linearly combined to solve one-shot analogy tasks with untrained spatial relations
weaknesses: Limited to single small architecture (OpenFlamingo-4B, 4B parameters)—unclear if findings generalize to larger contemporary LMMs with different training scales and modality fusion mechanisms
Scope restricted to spatial relations only (above/below/left/right)—no evidence approach generalizes to other semantic, functional, or social relations
Key analogy task results (Section 4.4) only demonstrated on synthetic data with highly controlled, simple spatial compositions; real-world compositional generalization unproven
Real-world dataset very small (201 images, 7 relations)—limits confidence in generalization claims and real-world applicability
Zero-shot baseline performance extremely low (~5-10% accuracy), making improvements easier to achieve and raising questions about whether gains reflect genuine relational understanding

Causal claims depend entirely on specific perturbation strategy (balancing four relation types exactly once); no sensitivity analysis or robustness checks provided for alternative perturbation schemes
Missing important baseline comparisons: no comparison to other activation steering approaches, LoRA fine-tuning, or other interpretability methods
Limited mechanistic insight—paper identifies which heads matter but provides minimal analysis of what computations these heads perform beyond 'encoding spatial relations'
Design choices lack justification: sum vs. average in Equation (2) not discussed; choice of top-10 heads appears arbitrary; softmax weighting in Equation (5) for composite vectors seems ad-hoc
Incremental novelty over Todd et al. (2024)—primarily an engineering adaptation of existing function vector technique rather than fundamental methodological innovation

strengths: Successfully extends function vectors from LLMs to multimodal settings with rigorous causal mediation analysis using Average Indirect Effect
Comprehensive experimental design with multiple datasets (synthetic and GQA), relation types (spatial and agentic), and evaluation paradigms (zero-shot intervention, fine-tuning, analogy)
Extensive ablation studies examining injection layer, head set size, and context size effects, demonstrating systematic investigation
Strong empirical improvements: fine-tuned vectors achieve >2× improvements over zero-shot baselines and consistently outperform 4-shot ICL across both models
Cross-dataset transfer experiments (Appendix F) show function vectors generalize across visual domains, suggesting robust relational structure learning
Clear presentation with well-motivated introduction and effective visualizations; thorough appendices with per-relation results and additional analyses
Novel use of adversarially-constructed uninformative context for causal perturbation is methodologically sound
weaknesses: Severely limited scope: only 4 spatial relations in synthetic dataset and 7 spatial + 5 agentic relations in GQA; no evidence that method scales to diverse real-world relation types (comparative, temporal, abstract relations)
Modest absolute performance levels: OpenFlamingo achieves only ~25% on synthetic dataset and ~40% on GQA Spatial even with fine-tuning; no human baselines provided to contextualize difficulty

Composite function vectors have limited practical applicability—require one-shot source example to compute weights and explicitly cannot be applied zero-shot; fundamentally contradicts claims about generalization to untrained relations

Model-specific behavior undermines generalizability: function vectors show divergent structures across OpenFlamingo (~0.9 cosine similarity between relations) vs. Qwen3-VL (negative correlations); negative RSA correlations (r=-0.38) suggest different relational encodings across models with no explanation provided

Limited mechanistic insight: paper identifies which attention heads matter but not what they compute; no analysis of whether heads specialize in particular relations or how spatial vs. agentic relations differ in attention space

Insufficient comparison with alternative methods: missing comparisons with other model intervention approaches (LoRA, direct head fine-tuning, other activation steering); no ablation comparing fine-tuned function vectors to fine-tuned random vectors or entire model fine-tuning

Fine-tuning lacks rigor: hyperparameters (10 epochs, lr=0.003) appear arbitrary without justification; no statistical significance testing or error bars; no ablation distinguishing value of causal initialization vs. fine-tuning itself on small datasets (1000-2100 examples)

Causal mediation analysis robustness not explored: perturbation strategy (uninformative context) is one choice among many; sensitivity to alternative perturbations not tested; AIE identifies influential heads but not their functional roles
Limited interpretability of vectors: no analysis of why intermediate layers are optimal or what relational structure is encoded; vectors used as black boxes without deeper investigation

Novel object generalization shows concerning model differences (OpenFlamingo 13.6% vs. Qwen3-VL 72.2%) that are unexplained; suggests object-specific information may be captured despite relation-focused claims

strengths: Comprehensive experimental methodology with careful ablation studies examining layer selection, head set size, and context size effects
Well-motivated investigation of relational reasoning in LMMs with clear presentation and informative visualizations
Evaluation on both synthetic and real image datasets (GQA) with tests of generalization to novel objects and cross-dataset transfer
Sound technical execution of causal mediation analysis using Average Indirect Effect (AIE) to identify influential attention heads
Appropriate use of zero-shot interventions to establish causality of extracted function vectors
weaknesses: Severe baseline performance issues raise fundamental task validity concerns: OpenFlamingo achieves only 9.7% on 4-shot synthetic (vs 25% random chance), and no human performance baseline is provided to contextualize difficulty
Limited technical novelty: primarily a straightforward application of Todd et al. (2024)'s function vector framework with minimal methodological adaptation for multimodal settings

Severely restricted experimental scope limited to 4 spatial relations (synthetic) and 12 total relations (GQA) with no evaluation on other relational categories, fundamentally limiting generalizability claims

Inconsistent generalization: cross-dataset transfer (Appendix F) shows transferred FVs underperform domain-specific vectors, and negative RSA correlations between models (r=-0.38) indicate fundamentally different internal relational geometries
Modest improvements from weak baselines: OpenFlamingo fine-tuned FVs reach ~30% accuracy (still far from human capability) and analogy improvements are from extremely low baselines (8.1%→16.8%)
Absent statistical analysis: no error bars, confidence intervals, significance testing, or discussion of variance across random seeds, making results reproducibility unclear
Limited model coverage: only two small models tested (OpenFlamingo-4B, Qwen3-VL-4B) with no evaluation on larger or more recent models, limiting assessment of scalability

Minimal mechanistic insight: beyond identifying important heads via AIE scores, the paper provides limited understanding of what function vectors represent or how different models process relations differently

Composite FV methodology concern: described as 'one-shot analogy' but requires source examples to compute weights via Eq. 5, conflating with in-context learning; hand-crafted mixtures dismissed without ablation

Weak baselines: no comparison to other interpretability/control methods for LMMs, parameter-efficient fine-tuning approaches (LoRA), or full task-specific fine-tuning that would serve as stronger baselines

strengths: Novel extension of function vector framework to multimodal domain with rigorous methodology for identifying and manipulating visual relational reasoning in LMMs
Comprehensive experimental design with proper ablations (injection layer, head set size, context size) across two models and both synthetic and real datasets
Demonstrates practical utility: fine-tuned function vectors significantly outperform in-context learning baselines while keeping model parameters frozen
Principled causal methodology using Average Indirect Effect (AIE) with perturbed prompts clearly identifies sparse, localized attention head subsets responsible for relation processing
Clear presentation with strong motivation, informative visualizations, and thorough appendix; good reproducibility with detailed dataset construction and promised code release
Honest treatment of limitations: authors openly discuss narrow relation coverage, low absolute performance, CFV constraints, and raise important questions about model-specific encoding geometries
Multiple validation settings: zero-shot intervention, fine-tuning on held-out data, cross-dataset transfer, and one-shot analogy tasks demonstrate robustness of approach
weaknesses: Limited scope of evaluated relations: only 4 spatial relations (synthetic) and 12 total relations (GQA Spatial + Agentic); physical and social relations acknowledged as future work, raising generalizability questions

Low absolute performance even with fine-tuned vectors (OpenFlamingo: ~44% on synthetic, Qwen3-VL: ~76%), questioning whether models truly understand relations versus memorizing patterns, and limiting practical applicability

Critical finding in Appendix G undermines universality claims: OpenFlamingo and Qwen3-VL encode relations in fundamentally different geometries (RSA correlation r = -0.38), suggesting findings may be model-specific rather than discovering universal relational knowledge

Composite function vectors (CFVs) severely limited by requirement for one-shot example to infer weights, negating zero-shot advantage; only demonstrated on four compositional relations rather than truly novel ones
Missing critical comparisons to alternative approaches: no comparison to LoRA fine-tuning, standard parameter-efficient methods, or other steering/intervention techniques on equivalent data budgets

Several design choices lack principled justification: selection of top-10 heads appears arbitrary (though Figure 12 shows range), different injection layers (19 vs 8) unexplained, perturbed context mixing lacks ablation
Limited model coverage: only 4B parameter models tested; scalability to larger/smaller models unknown, and architectural differences between OpenFlamingo and Qwen3-VL noted but not analyzed
Task specificity concerns: highly constrained relation task (query object → answer object) doesn't capture richer relational reasoning scenarios; generalization to complex reasoning unclear
Statistical rigor issues: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or analysis of variance across relations and random seeds; results lack error quantification
